flashcards.back: One who does their duty without attachment to its results, not one who only gives up work or rituals.
For the seeker, Karma-yoga is the means to calm; once yoga is reached, calmness becomes the means to Self-realization.
The mind is the friend of those who control it and the enemy of those who don't. Lift yourself by your own mind.
One who has mastered mind and senses stays calm in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
Superior is one impartial to friends, enemies, neutrals, haters, relatives, saints and sinners.
A clean, quiet place; spine, neck and head erect; gaze steady; mind and senses restrained.
Yoga fails for those who eat or sleep too much or too little. Moderation in all things is needed.
When the disciplined mind is free of all desire and rests in the Self, one is united with the Eternal.
A lamp in a windless place does not flicker: so is the yogi's mind, sheltered from desire.
After Self-realization one sees no gain as higher, and is not shaken by even the greatest sorrow.
Severing the union with sorrow: practised with firm resolve and without doubt.
Just witness it, under the supervision of the Self, and bring it gently back.

flashcards.front: How is the restless mind subdued? (6.35)
flashcards.back: By constant, vigorous practice with perseverance, Self-knowledge and detachment.
One who regards every being like oneself and feels others' pain and pleasure as their own.
Carried toward God by past practice; even the seeker of yoga surpasses those who only perform rituals.
The yogi-devotee who lovingly contemplates God with supreme faith, mind ever absorbed in him.

quiz.text: Who is the true renunciant in Chapter 6?

options.B: One who works without attachment to results
options.C: One who lives in a forest

quiz.why: Renunciation is of selfish motive, not of duty.

quiz.text: The mind is the enemy of whom?

options.B: Of those who don't control it

quiz.why: 6.5-6: controlled, it is a friend; uncontrolled, an enemy.

quiz.text: What is needed for success in yoga, regarding food and sleep?
quiz.why: Too much or too little of either makes yoga fail.

quiz.text: The steady mind is compared to:

options.B: A lamp in a windless place

quiz.why: It does not flicker when sheltered from desire.

quiz.text: When the mind wanders in meditation, one should:

options.C: Witness it and bring it back to the Self

quiz.text: How is yoga defined in this chapter?
Who is the best yogi in 6.32?

options.B: One who feels others' pain and joy as their own

quiz.text: Who is best of all yogis (6.47)?

options.A: No gain seems higher, and sorrow cannot shake one
